title: When the Inheritance Falls
premise: Tamsin Winterbourne, a night dispatcher for a failing taxi company, receives a prepaid fare from a stranger who asks her to prove his sister's murder never happened — because the body was never found and the family insists she's alive. Pulling on the thread, Tamsin discovers the 'dead' woman was the family's black sheep, hidden away after threatening to expose how the Winterbourne-adjacent Ashgrove fortune was really made. The witness everyone swears is dead is alive, and the anniversary dinner is the deadline: the will's final clause expires that night. Tamsin must choose between the loyalty of the only people who ever made her feel she belonged and the truth that will burn their world down — and she chooses truth, exposing the patriarch's fraud and finding her own place outside the family that used her.
about_author: F. M. Voss spent a decade answering phones for a night-shift taxi dispatch before turning to fiction, and the voices in this book are all ones she heard through a headset. She writes from a rented room above a depot, where the radios never quite go silent.

chapters.title: Prepaid, No Destination
chapters.summary: Tamsin, night dispatcher, takes an odd booking: a man pays triple to be driven to Ashgrove House and back, asking only that she confirm no one there has died. POV Tamsin. Emotional beat: wary curiosity — she's seen every kind of fare, never one that pays to disprove a murder.

chapters.title: The Client Who Waits
chapters.summary: The client, Elias Marsh, explains his sister Vivian supposedly died a year ago, but there's no body, no inquest, no grave — only a death notice. He wants Tamsin's insider access to the family's taxi accounts, which Vivian once worked through. POV Tamsin. Beat: reluctant agreement; the money is too good and the hole in the story too clean.

chapters.title: Ashgrove House at 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: Tamsin drives Elias to the estate; the house is lit for a party a year early — the anniversary dinner. A woman at a window watches them leave, and Tamsin swears it's the face from Vivian's old employee photo. POV Tamsin. Beat: first real dread; the case stops being hypothetical.

chapters.title: Company Cards, Company Secrets
chapters.summary: Digging through dispatch logs, Tamsin finds Vivian's old runs: repeated midnight fares to a solicitor's office and a shuttered mill, all expensed by the family patriarch, Alistair Ashgrove. POV Tamsin. Beat: the thrill of competence — invisibility has its uses after all.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Guest List
chapters.summary: Elias reveals the will's clause: Alistair's fortune passes fully only after the anniversary dinner, unless Vivian appears to contest it. The family has every reason to keep her 'dead.' POV Elias. Beat: stakes sharpen — a clock is now running.

chapters.title: Old Routes
chapters.summary: Tamsin retraces Vivian's midnight route to the mill and finds a padlocked office with fresh tire tracks. Someone still visits. POV Tamsin. Beat: fear braided with resolve; she's no longer observing.

chapters.title: The Family That Took Her In
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: how the Ashgroves' driver, Ruth, gave teenage runaway Tamsin her first job and first sense of belonging. POV Tamsin. Beat: tenderness and debt — the loyalty she'll be asked to betray.

chapters.title: Ruth Lies Badly
chapters.summary: Tamsin asks Ruth about Vivian; Ruth's denial is too fast, and she begs Tamsin to let the anniversary pass quietly. POV Ruth. Beat: the first crack — a protector protecting something.

chapters.title: Death Notice, No Death
chapters.summary: Tamsin pulls the newspaper notice and finds it was placed by the family solicitor, Prentice, with no coroner's reference. Elias is followed home and warns her off. POV Elias. Beat: the investigation acquires teeth and enemies.

chapters.title: The Mill at Midnight
chapters.summary: Tamsin stakes out the mill and sees Prentice deliver an envelope to a woman who never steps into the light. She loses him in the fog. POV Tamsin. Beat: confirmation — the witness is alive, and someone is paying for her silence.

chapters.title: Alistair's Toast
chapters.summary: Invited under a pretext to Ashgrove House, Tamsin meets Alistair, who is charming, dying, and clearly knows who she is. He offers her Ruth's job if she stops asking. POV Alistair. Beat: seduction of belonging versus the itch of truth.

chapters.title: What the Fortune Was Built On
chapters.summary: Elias and Tamsin find the mill's history: it was a workers' housing scheme Alistair converted to speculative flats, ruining dozens — Vivian was the bookkeeper who kept the real ledgers. POV Elias. Beat: the murder question inverts; Vivian was never killed, she was bought.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Tamsin locates the second ledger hidden in the depot's dead-file, in Vivian's handwriting — and a note naming the person she trusted with it. The name is Ruth. POV Tamsin. Beat: betrayal lands close; her anchor is compromised.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Break Room
chapters.summary: Ruth admits she held the ledger for Vivian but swears she doesn't know where Vivian is now — and that Alistair's son Marcus has been asking the same questions, less gently. POV Ruth. Beat: guilt and fear; loyalty revealed as a cage.

chapters.title: Marcus
chapters.summary: Marcus Ashgrove corners Tamsin, friendly and lethal, revealing he knows about Elias and offering to split whatever the ledger proves — provided Vivian stays gone. POV Marcus. Beat: the antagonist steps forward; the danger turns personal.

chapters.title: Elias Doesn't Come Home
chapters.summary: Elias vanishes after a prepaid fare to the mill is logged from his own phone. Tamsin finds his room searched, the sister's photos gone. POV Tamsin. Beat: guilt and terror — her ally has paid for her curiosity.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Window
chapters.summary: Following the depot's own GPS ghosts, Tamsin traces a car registered to the estate to a coastal caravan park — and finds Vivian Marsh alive, hiding, half-feral, refusing to return. POV Vivian. Beat: the witness found, but broken; truth is not the same as rescue.

chapters.title: Vivian's Account
chapters.summary: Vivian tells her side: she faked the notice to escape Alistair's leverage, but Marcus has been hunting the ledger to erase the last proof, and she believes he has Elias. She'll only come forward if Tamsin gets the ledger out first. POV Vivian. Beat: alliance forged under duress.

chapters.title: The Exchange at the Mill
chapters.summary: Tamsin offers Marcus the ledger's location for Elias; the handover goes wrong, Prentice turns on Marcus, and in the chaos Tamsin grabs both the ledger and a concussed Elias. POV Tamsin. Beat: climax begins — violence, reversal, narrow escape.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: At Ashgrove House, as glasses rise to the dead woman, Tamsin walks in with the ledger and Vivian beside her. Alistair, confronted before the family, confesses the scheme to end it; Marcus is taken by police waiting outside; Ruth stands by Tamsin, finally. POV Tamsin. Beat: climax and catharsis — truth spoken at the family's own table.

chapters.title: What the Will Decides
chapters.summary: The will's clause honored, Vivian redirects the fortune to the mill workers' restitution fund and settles Elias's debts. Alistair dies within the month, unrepentant but unmasked. POV Elias. Beat: justice without triumphalism; the cost is counted honestly.

chapters.title: Day Shift
chapters.summary: Tamsin declines a management job and stays on nights — but now by choice, with Ruth as her dispatcher partner and a life no longer built on invisibility. A new odd fare comes in; she takes it, smiling. POV Tamsin. Beat: belonging earned, not inherited; the door left open.
